Title: Malaysia, Pakistan to boost cooperation in fight against narcotics
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on narcotics cooperation will provide a more structured framework to strengthen existing collaboration between Malaysia and Pakistan in addressing current drug threats, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said discussions on the MoU were held during his visit to the Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) Pakistan headquarters in Islamabad yesterday, where he received a briefing from its director-general, Major General Abdul Moeed.
Drug threats have become increasingly complex, particularly with the rise of synthetic drugs such as methamphetamine and the involvement of transnational organised crime networks operating across borders.
"Pakistan's position, which directly faces drug flows from Afghanistan, makes cooperation with the country important for Malaysia, especially as trafficking routes extend to East Asia and Southeast Asia.
"We cannot address this threat only within national borders or the Asean region," he said in a Facebook post in conjunction with his two-day official visit to Islamabad, which began on Thursday (Aug 20).
He said that in dealing with increasingly sophisticated criminal networks, cooperation between enforcement agencies must go beyond agreements on paper, with intelligence sharing, coordinated intelligence-led operations and international networks being utilised to disrupt supply chains before drugs reach Malaysia.
Malaysia and Pakistan already have a strong operational foundation, including more than 28 cases jointly coordinated between 2012 and 2018.
He said future efforts would focus on revitalising cooperation through more active intelligence sharing, coordinated intelligence-led operations, and training and expertise exchanges between agencies from both countries.
During the visit, Saifuddin also paid a courtesy call on Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, with discussions covering regional and international developments, the role of dialogue and diplomacy in addressing conflicts, and the need to strengthen cooperation among Islamic countries in addressing current geopolitical and economic challenges.
The discussions also covered economic cooperation, including trade and investment, food security involving potential rice and meat supplies from Pakistan, market access and efforts to enhance people-to-people ties through proposed visa facilitation.
He also held a meeting with his counterpart, Pakistan's Interior and Narcotics Control Minister Syed Mohsin Raza Naqvi, where both sides agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to further develop cooperation in security, narcotics control and police training.
The meeting also witnessed the signing of the International Transfer of Prisoners Agreement between Malaysia and Pakistan.
Saifuddin and the Malaysian delegation also visited the headquarters of Pakistan's National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) to observe the country's identity management and civil registration systems.
The delegation was briefed by Nadra chairman Lieutenant General Muhammad Munir Afsar on identity databases, biometrics, the use of technology in government service delivery, border management, passport data verification, digital identity and support for law enforcement efforts.
He said the visit opened opportunities for cooperation and expertise sharing in digital identity solutions, e-government, crisis management and cybersecurity.
The experience would be useful as the Home Ministry explores the use of technology to enhance security and improve system efficiency, in line with the Madani government's efforts to ensure public sector digital transformation delivers direct benefits to the people.

Title: US, Canada fail to reach trade pact to avert Trump tariffs
Article:
WASHINGTON: Hefty US tariffs on some Canadian products took effect on Saturday after days of negotiations that went down to the wire failed to produce an agreement.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney vowed that his country would match the US tariffs "dollar for dollar to protect our workers and businesses", after officials said late Friday that Washington and Ottawa had not managed to strike a deal.
The lack of a final agreement means that new 50 per cent duties, set to impact some US$20 billion of Canadian exports to the United States, took effect on Saturday.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told reporters on Friday that "tonight, Canada declined to finalise the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week".
That came despite Washington's offers for tariff reductions in sectors such as steel and aluminium, he added.
The surprise announcement came after Trump said that the United States "should be able to have a deal with Canada", citing his "good relationship" with Carney.
After hours of trade talks on Friday, however, Canada's top negotiator Dominic LeBlanc told reporters that officials still "have more work to do".
LeBlanc and Greer also met for around three hours on Thursday.
Greer said the Trump administration put on the table "significant tariff reductions on steel, aluminum, autos and lumber" in exchange for concessions from Canada.
He said Canada was also maintaining its "prolonged retaliation" against the United States.
But Carney said in a statement that "last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal".
'DISCRIMINATORY TREATMENT'
Canada's regional leaders said previously that the United States was particularly irritated by one retaliatory measure: the removal of US alcohol and wine from liquor stores.
The White House had alleged "discriminatory treatment" by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products in introducing the duties.
They were originally set to take effect on Wednesday, before Trump issued a last-minute delay of three days – citing major progress in talks.
Canadian negotiators have been camped out in Washington this week to firm up a deal that aimed to address various flash points.
Canada has been seeking relief from Trump's tariffs on autos, steel and aluminium, which have battered the country's economy, forced job losses and strained what was once an iron-clad trade relationship.
Carney has repeatedly told Canadians that relations with the United States have been forever changed, regardless of what happens with an individual trade deal.
He says the country must diversify and reduce its reliance on the United States, which currently accounts for roughly 70 per cent of Canadian exports.
Beyond the ongoing negotiations, the United States and Canada still have to agree on revisions to the North American free trade agreement, USMCA, which Trump declined to renew last month.

Title: Safe internet campaign highlights parental role, social media ban for under-16s - Teo
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Efforts to raise parents' awareness of the ban on social media accounts for children under 16 will be intensified through the Safe Internet Campaign, said Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching.
She said the message would be a major focus of the government's efforts to ensure parents more closely monitor and guide their children's use of digital devices.
She said that although parents were still allowed to register digital accounts for their children, preventive measures and self-regulation at home were critical to complying with the government's current policy.
"This is one of the key messages we want to convey to parents. The current Madani government policy is that children aged 16 and below should not have social media accounts.
"It is not just about (parents) prohibiting them, but more importantly, educating and guiding (their children).
"Parents need to take responsibility for monitoring online activities and ensuring that devices such as mobile phones or tablets provided to their children are not misused," she said at a press conference during the Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) Convention for the Safe Internet Campaign at the Sri Tebrau Multipurpose Hall here today.
On enforcement, Teo said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) would take follow-up action on reports of misuse of accounts involving minors by referring them to digital platform providers for the removal of the accounts.
The fourth instalment of the Safe Internet Campaign in Johor today, which focused on the role of PTAs, served as the main platform to broaden understanding of the issue before the campaign roadshow moves to Sabah in September and Sarawak in October.
On the campaign's achievements to date, Teo said the programme had been implemented extensively, involving thousands of educational institutions nationwide.
These included 5,946 Sekolah Kebangsaan, 2,416 Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan, 1,285 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina and 524 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil.
In addition to primary and secondary schools, the campaign has also been conducted at 68 institutions of higher learning, 67 Form Six or vocational colleges and six teacher education institutes.
Malaysia began enforcing age-verification requirements for social media account registration on June 1 under the Child Protection Code and Risk Mitigation Code, implemented by MCMC pursuant to the Online Safety Act 2025.
Under the regulations, individuals under 16 are not allowed to open social media accounts, while users are required to verify their identities using official documents such as the MyKad, passport or MyDigital ID.

Title: Immigration truck crash survivor keeps asking for husband who died
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A woman who survived a fatal crash involving an Immigration Department truck in Jalan Sultan Ismail has been asking for her husband, unaware that he died in the accident.
A woman known as Arda shared that Norhayati Razali, 55, was still asking why her husband, Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, had yet to visit her in hospital.
Arda's daughter, Udik, is friends with Norhayati and Shaik's daughter, Siti Darwisyah, 12, who was also killed in the crash, along with her older sister, Siti Nor Sazlin, 25.
Arda shared a video of Udik recounting her visit to Norhayati, who suffered head, hand and leg injuries, at Kuala Lumpur Hospital.
Speaking through tears in the video, Udik said they showed Norhayati photos of those who died in the crash.
"But she still does not remember," the teenager said.
"She asked why her husband had not come to visit her."
The 1am crash on Wednesday happened after Shaik's family were hit by an out-of-control truck while walking near the Maju Junction traffic light intersection.
On Thursday, the driver of the Immigration truck,
Mohd Akbar Zainol, was charged
in the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate's Court with five offences.
These included three charges under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act for causing the deaths of the three family members, and one charge under Section 43(1) of the same act for reckless and inconsiderate driving resulting in injuries to Norhayati.
He pleaded not guilty to all charges and was granted bail of RM60,000.

Title: Sara initiative boosts sales for Sabah retailers, wholesalers and manufacturers
Article:
SEMPORNA: The Rahmah Basic Contribution (Sara) initiative is generating wider economic benefits in Sabah, with retailers, wholesalers and local manufacturers recording higher sales as more businesses join the programme and locally made products are added to its redemption list.
The expansion of Sara Merchant Partners, which now involves 1,495 businesses in Sabah, together with the "Kami Support Produk Lokal Sabah" initiative, has increased sales among local entrepreneurs by between 50 and 80 per cent while strengthening demand for locally produced goods.
Koperasi Anugerah Haji Badli chairman Sobri Lawdji said joining the Sara Merchant Partner programme late last year had significantly benefited the cooperative, which was established in early 2024 and is the only Sara Merchant Partner on Pulau Bum-Bum, Semporna.
He said daily sales rose sharply, especially at the beginning of each month when recipients received their assistance, with essential items such as rice, sugar, cooking oil, flour and onions among the best-selling products.
"Supplies have never run out, including during festive seasons, as we ensure sufficient stocks are prepared in advance," he said.
Sobri said the initiative had benefited more than 25,000 residents on the island who are eligible for Sara For All, including 3,300 recipients eligible for Sara Monthly and Rahmah Cash Aid (STR).
He added that the cooperative also organised Rahmah Madani Sales to support island residents, many of whom work as fishermen and face income challenges during periods of strong winds.
Sobri hoped Sara would continue and that its allocation could be increased to further empower local retailers while easing the burden on island communities.
He said previously, residents had to spend up to RM50 on transport to travel by boat for about 15 minutes to Semporna town to purchase essential goods.
Meanwhile, Dpro Trading Sdn Bhd director in Tawau, Tham Nyuk Lin, said the wholesale and retail business, which she has operated since 2017, recorded encouraging sales growth after joining Sara late last year.
She said customers' purchasing power increased significantly whenever the assistance was distributed, with rice being the most sought-after item, followed by sugar, cooking oil and local products.
Besides direct sales to consumers, her Tawau premises also attracted small retailers who purchased bulk supplies worth between RM500 and RM600 for resale.
"Our shop offers affordable prices, so small traders prefer to source their supplies here. This allows them to resell the goods or use them to produce other products at lower prices in their respective areas," she said.
Tham said overall supplies at the store remained sufficient, with only minimal delays caused by disruptions in supplier deliveries.
She hoped the Sara programme would continue as it had helped boost local businesses while enabling lower-income groups to obtain essential goods.
For local manufacturers, Rich Inspiration Sdn Bhd marketing officer Arsiyati Mando said the listing of the company's products under Sara had increased sales for the Tawau-based business.
She said several essential products under the local Magic Cook brand, including corn flour, tapioca flour, soy sauce and sauces, had been included in the Sara product list since the initiative was introduced by the government in August last year.
"Participation in Sara has greatly supported our company, especially amid the current economic situation. The increase in sales is evident as customers prioritise products that can be purchased through the programme," she said.
Arsiyati said the initiative provided dual benefits by helping B40 households obtain quality kitchen essentials while supporting the growth of Sabah's local manufacturing sector.
She hoped the government would continue Sara and expand the range of local products eligible for redemption to create more growth opportunities for local entrepreneurs.

Title: Malaysia calls for collective Asean action to tackle transboundary haze
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia is calling for collective action by all Asean member states to strengthen preparedness in addressing the risk of transboundary haze.
This includes preventive measures, national preparedness and continuous monitoring, in line with the principles of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP).
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said all member states needed to strengthen control measures and preparedness by closely monitoring high-risk areas, enhancing hotspot surveillance, enforcing the ban on open burning and ensuring efficient firefighting readiness.
He said Malaysia's position was conveyed in an official message to Asean Secretary-General Dr Kao Kim Hourn yesterday.
Arthur said that although fire incidents remained under control within the respective borders of member states, the risk of transboundary haze called for collective preparedness and heightened vigilance at the regional level.
"The implementation of early interventions, accurate information exchange and close regional coordination are fundamental elements in addressing the haze issue effectively," he said in a statement today.
He said monitoring of current weather developments showed that prolonged dry conditions in southern areas of the Asean region had resulted in an increase in hotspot activity and haze.
"This situation risks becoming more widespread as the El Nino phenomenon is expected to gradually strengthen over the coming months," he said.
Arthur said Malaysia also welcomed the proactive role of the Asean Secretariat as the Interim Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control (ACC THPC) in facilitating information dissemination, coordinating preparedness measures among member states and strengthening cooperation mechanisms under the AATHP.
"Malaysia is confident that the strong commitment and proactive actions of all Asean member states will enhance regional resilience in confronting climate challenges, while safeguarding a sustainable, prosperous and haze-free environment for the well-being of present and future generations," he said.

Title: Malaysia, 11 countries condemn Israeli strikes on Syria
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and 11 other countries have strongly condemned Israeli airstrikes targeting the Abu al-Duhur military airbase in northwestern Syria, describing the attacks as "an extreme escalation" and "a flagrant violation" of Syria's sovereignty, territorial integrity and political unity.
In a joint statement on Friday, the foreign ministers of Malaysia, Turkiye, Algeria, Indonesia, Jordan, Lebanon, Mauritania, Pakistan, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Somalia expressed deep concern over the continued targeting and destruction of Syria's territory and infrastructure.
"These attacks constitute an extreme escalation and a flagrant violation of the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political unity of the Syrian Arab Republic," the statement said.
The ministers warned that such actions risk directly undermining Syria's efforts to restore security, rebuild national institutions and address the humanitarian consequences of years of prolonged conflict.
They stressed that Israel's continued violations of Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity risk further escalating tensions, undermining regional peace and stability, and eroding respect for international law and the principles of the United Nations (UN) Charter.
The ministers called on the international community to adopt "a firm, clear and principled position" in response to what they described as continued aggression against Syria.
They also urged the international community to take "concrete steps, in accordance with international law and the UN Charter, to bring an end to these violations".
The ministers specifically called for "full respect for the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the areas they have occupied", saying such measures were necessary "to prevent further escalation and protect regional peace and stability".
The 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement between Syria and Israel established a buffer zone and separation of forces following the 1973 Arab-Israeli war, with the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) deployed to monitor its implementation.
The ministers also underscored "the imperative of respect for Syria's sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and political unity" and stressed their rejection of "any attempt to undermine them".
The joint statement comes amid heightened regional tensions, with the 12 countries warning that continued military action against Syrian territory could further threaten peace and stability in the region.
The ministers reiterated that respect for international law and the UN Charter remains essential to preventing further escalation and safeguarding regional peace and stability.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: LPG cylinders explode after lorry catches fire on SILK Highway
Article:
KAJANG: A lorry driver escaped unhurt while his attendant suffered burns after a lorry carrying gas cylinders caught fire before several cylinders exploded at Km0.1 of the SILK Highway yesterday.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said preliminary investigations showed that the lorry was travelling towards Semenyih when the incident occurred about 4.40pm.
"Upon reaching Km0.1 of the SILK Highway, the 55-year-old lorry driver noticed that the gas cylinders being transported had caught fire.
"The driver immediately stopped the vehicle on the road shoulder and managed to escape.
"As a result of the incident, the load on the lorry continued to burn, causing some of the gas cylinders to explode and be hurled across the road," Naazron said in a statement.
A video of the incident has since gone viral on social media.
Naazron said the lorry was completely destroyed by fire.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department state operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Ashbar, in a separate statement, said the lorry, which was carrying liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders, was about 98 per cent destroyed in the incident.
He said the lorry attendant suffered burns in the incident, while the driver escaped unhurt.
He added that eight personnel, along with a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) and Emergency Medical Rescue Service (EMRS) unit from the Bangi Fire and Rescue Station, were dispatched to the scene.
"The operations commander reported that a three-tonne lorry carrying LPG cylinders had caught fire, and firefighting operations were immediately carried out to prevent the blaze from spreading," he said.
He also said the cause of the fire and the extent of the losses were still under investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar, Sheikh Al-Azhar discuss efforts to deepen understanding of Islam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sheikh al-Azhar al-Sharif Prof Dr Ahmad al-Tayyeb discussed continuing dakwah efforts and Islamic studies to deepen religious understanding for the benefit of the wider community.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said the matter was discussed during a phone call after the prominent cleric contacted him to enquire about his health and offer prayers following his recovery from surgery.
"I greatly appreciate his prayers and thoughts and informed him that the surgery went smoothly, while my recovery is also going very well, thank God.
"We also talked about continuing dakwah and study efforts to deepen the understanding of Islam.
"His views and guidance will continue to be an important reference in upholding the noble tradition of Islamic knowledge and bringing blessings to the entire community," he said in the post.
Anwar said he also brought up Sheikh al-Azhar al-Sharif's previous visit to Malaysia, which had left a deep impression on Muslims in the country.
"We hope to meet again in Cairo or Kuala Lumpur to continue our dakwah efforts and expand knowledge for the benefit of the entire community," he said.
In a separate post, Anwar said he also spoke with Council of Muslim Elders Secretary-General Mohamed Abdelsalam, who enquired about his health and offered prayers following his surgery.
Anwar said he also asked about Mohamed's wife, who is currently receiving treatment in hospital, and prayed for her speedy recovery.
"We then touched on the desire of Sheikh al-Azhar al-Sharif, Prof Dr Ahmad al-Tayyeb, to return to Malaysia, as well as several new initiatives, especially to strengthen Malaysia's relationship with al-Azhar and nurture the idea of a simple, free and authoritative Islam.
"I greatly appreciate the friendship, support and trust shown by Mohamed Abdelsalam and Sheikh al-Azhar al-Sharif," he said.
Anwar said he was also touched by the appreciation expressed by his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, who described him as an exemplary figure for his steadfastness, loyalty and sacrifices throughout his struggle.
"All these endeavours and cooperation will continue to be strengthened for the benefit of the people and universal well-being," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Patriotic creations turn sewing hobby into income for Kuala Krai woman
Article:
KUALA KRAI: Her colourful patriotic-themed creations, which blend the Jalur Gemilang's red, white, yellow and blue with traditional attire, have turned a sewing hobby into a growing source of income for 47-year-old Aimi Aidora Ramli.
Her creativity in producing patriotic-themed and traditional clothing representing various races has received an encouraging response, particularly from parents who want their children to wear unique outfits for competitions and programmes held in conjunction with National Day celebrations.
Aimi Aidora said that while she previously produced only a few sets of patriotic-themed clothing, this year she had successfully completed 12 sets of traditional women's clothing and three sets of men's clothing representing various races, including Malays, Chinese and Indians.
"Initially, I only sewed children's clothes using the Jalur Gemilang colours as a hobby. However, when I received positive feedback from customers, I started adding traditional clothing from various races to my collection to give students more choices.
"An interest in sewing and the desire to instil a sense of patriotism among children were the main drivers behind me producing clothes with an Independence Day theme," she said.
She said the clothing collection not only met customer demand but also served as a medium to highlight Malaysia's cultural diversity and spirit of unity, especially during National Day and Malaysia Day celebrations.
"I started thinking about expanding this business further because it is quite difficult for people in Kuala Krai to find rental clothes with retro and patriotic themes.
"Apart from maintaining my existing rental collection, I also sew clothes according to customers' orders at prices ranging from RM45 to RM65, including accessories, depending on the pattern and design chosen," she said.
Aimi Aidora, who also accepts orders for flower arrangements for handout trays, said she had so far received orders from students who wanted to wear the outfits for National Day celebrations at their schools.
She said demand was expected to continue increasing until the middle of next month.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perak youth urged to bridge skills gap as investments surge
Article:
IPOH: Perak's youth must equip themselves with the skills needed to take advantage of thousands of job opportunities expected to be created as the state's economy continues to expand.
Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the state's economy grew by 5.7 per cent to RM91.5 billion last year, while the manufacturing sector recorded growth of 15.2 per cent.
"Approved investments also reached RM15.76 billion and are expected to create 10,704 job opportunities," he said.
Saarani said this in his speech at the opening of the fifth session of the Perak Youth Assembly at Bangunan Perak Darul Ridzuan here today.
However, Saarani said the key question was whether Perakians, especially the state's youth, would be ready to fill those positions.
"Whenever figures like these are presented to me, there is one thing I always think about: how many of those opportunities will eventually be filled by the children of Perak?" he said.
He said the state government wanted to see Perakians benefit directly from the state's economic expansion, including through employment and business opportunities.
"We want that when industries grow, Perakians work in them, local entrepreneurs become part of their supply chains and more young people have the opportunity to build their future in their own state," he said.
Saarani said the state's five growth nodes, namely the Automotive High Technology Valley (AHTV) in Tanjung Malim, Lumut Maritime Industrial City (LuMIC), Kerian Integrated Green Industrial Park (KIGIP), Silver Valley Technology Park (SVTP) and Perak Halal Industrial Park (Perak HIP), were more than just development projects.
"These are where we are building some of the jobs and opportunities for the people of Perak," he said.
He said, however, that creating employment opportunities alone was insufficient if young people lacked information about the jobs available or the skills required by industries.
"If our young people do not know what jobs are being created, we have an information gap. If they know about them but do not have the necessary skills, we have a skills gap.
"And if they already have the skills but still find it difficult to enter the industry, we need to understand what is holding them back," he said.
Saarani said the Perak Youth Council could play an important role in identifying such gaps as its members were close to students choosing their career paths, graduates seeking employment and young people looking to start businesses.
"Reach out to them, listen to their experiences and identify what remains a barrier for young people in Perak to seize the opportunities available," he said.
Saarani also said the state did not want a situation where employment opportunities were available but local youths were unprepared to take them.
"We do not want the day to come when opportunities are already right in front of us, but the young people of Perak are not ready to seize them," he said.
Meanwhile, Saarani said the state government had increased the allocation for the fifth session of the Perak Youth Assembly from RM400,000 to RM600,000.
He said the additional allocation reflected the state's expectation that the council would strengthen its efforts and deliver a more meaningful impact for young people in Perak.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Mak Siti' gold mining syndicate making RM13,000 a day busted
Article:
MARANG: An illegal gold mining syndicate earning up to RM13,000 a day was busted after police detained 15 people in a raid at Bukit Kor.
The General Operations Force (GOF) also seized mining equipment and heavy machinery worth an estimated RM449,000 during the operation.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said those detained were four Malaysian men and 11 foreigners aged between 20 and 40.
The foreigners comprised 10 Cambodians and a Vietnamese.
Preliminary investigations found that the operation, spanning 4.05ha, had been running for about a month and was led by a Cambodian woman known as "Mak Siti".
"We seized a heavy machine, eight water pumps, three generators, two gold screening machines and a rock crusher," he told a press conference at the site.
Radzi said the syndicate excavated pits about 6m deep before crushing, washing, filtering and screening the material to extract gold.
The gold was sold to a local buyer known as "Pak Lang".
He said the syndicate could extract up to 40g of gold a day.
"This shows that illegal gold mining in Bukit Kor is no longer a small-scale operation, but involves an organised chain covering excavation, processing, gold extraction and marketing," Radzi said.
He added that the landowner was also being probed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teacher, 6-year-old son killed after MPV skids into ditch
Article:
KUANTAN: A teacher and her 6-year-old son were killed after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) they were travelling in skidded at Km149 of Jalan Kuantan-Seremban near Kampung Bukit Serok, Muadzam Shah, here yesterday.
The woman's husband, who was driving the MPV, suffered serious injuries in the 9.30pm accident.
District police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the family of three was travelling from Seremban, Negri Sembilan, to Felda Keratong 1 in Muadzam Shah when the incident occurred.
"Preliminary investigations showed that the MPV was believed to have hit a piece of wood on the road, causing the vehicle to lose control and skid into a ditch on the right side of the road," he said in a statement today.
Sharif Shai said Kartine Ngatenan, 46, a teacher at a school in Seremban, and her son, Muhammad Akif Mohd Azmi, six, were trapped in the vehicle and died at the scene.
The MPV driver, Mohd Azmi Mohahir, 47, was seriously injured and is receiving treatment at Muadzam Shah Hospital here.
Meanwhile, Pahang Fire and Rescue Department public relations officer Zulfadli Zakaria said a team from the Muadzam Shah Fire and Rescue Station rushed to the scene after receiving a report about the accident at 9.56pm.
"Upon arrival, we found that the teacher was trapped in the front passenger seat of the MPV, while her son was trapped in the rear passenger seat.
"Firefighters had to cut open the MPV using rescue equipment to remove the bodies of the mother and son," he said.
The bodies were sent to Muadzam Shah Hospital for post-mortem examinations. The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign worker applications now fully online from today
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Employers seeking to recruit foreign workers will no longer need to submit applications manually or make walk-in visits to government offices, with the entire process now conducted online through the Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS).
The Human Resources Ministry said the digitalisation of the application process, which takes effect today, was aimed at reducing repeated visits to government offices, shortening waiting times and making the process more organised and transparent.
However, the ministry said the move did not mean that requirements for hiring foreign workers had been relaxed.
"All applications remain subject to scrutiny, relevant laws, eligibility requirements, foreign worker employment policies and reviews by the relevant regulatory agencies," it said in a statement.
The ministry said the application process begins with employers obtaining prior approval to hire foreign workers under Section 60K of the Employment Act 1955, and ends with the issuance of a Conditional Approval Letter (SKB).
The SKB can be obtained within 14 days, subject to complete applications and compliance with the stipulated requirements and criteria. Employers can access FWCMS through www.fwcms.com.my (http://www.fwcms.com.my/).
Meanwhile, the ministry said a phased quota allocation approach was being implemented to facilitate employers' applications following the opening of a quota for 15,000 foreign workers in the restaurant industry, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on July 24.
"Of the quota, 5,000 foreign workers involving 1,033 employers who have undergone case-by-case interviews are being processed for approval," the statement said.
The ministry advised employers who had completed interviews or wished to submit new applications to complete the process through FWCMS.
In a related development, the ministry said the proposal to establish a Foreign Worker Transit Centre to address congestion involving foreign worker arrivals at Kuala Lumpur International Airport was being refined and would be introduced through a pilot project in the future.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pick-up truck crashes into house after hitting motorcycle
Article:
GUA MUSANG: A pick-up truck skidded and hit a motorcycle before crashing into a house along Jalan Kampung Kerinting here yesterday.
In the 4.55pm incident, the 53-year-old motorcyclist suffered injuries to his left leg and was treated at Gua Musang Hospital.
District police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo said the black Ford, driven by a 34-year-old man, was travelling from Cameron Highlands to Kota Baru.
He said the vehicle lost control upon reaching the location and hit the motorcyclist, who was stopped on the left shoulder of the road.
"As a result of the collision, the four-wheel-drive vehicle skidded before crashing into a house on the left side of the road.
"The motorcyclist suffered minor injuries to his left leg and is still receiving treatment at Gua Musang Hospital," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCBA foils attempt to smuggle 45 animal horns through Penang airport
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) has foiled an attempt to smuggle 45 pieces of suspected animal horns worth RM5,000 through Penang International Airport.
The seizure was made on Thursday following a baggage inspection involving a 57-year-old Indonesian man who had arrived from Guangzhou, China.
The passenger was found carrying the suspected wildlife products without a permit or valid documentation, an offence under Section 68(1)(b) of the Wildlife Conservation Act.
MCBA said all the seized items had been handed over to the Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) for investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Prince Harry and others ordered to pay millions over failed lawsuit
Article:
LONDON: Britain's Prince Harry, singer Elton John and other high-profile claimants face paying millions of dollars out of their own pockets to cover the legal costs of the Daily Mail's publisher after a judge ruled their failed privacy lawsuits were conducted in an unreasonable way.
Judge Matthew Nicklin's judgment on costs, published on Friday, ordered an interim payment from the claimants of £9.54 million, due by August 28, towards the legal costs of Associated Newspapers.
In a further damaging blow, Nicklin said the additional costs should be paid on an "indemnity basis", meaning Associated does not need to show they were reasonable and proportionate.
Last month, Nicklin comprehensively rejected the case brought by King Charles' younger son, John and five other figures, rejecting allegations that the Mail titles had engaged in widespread unlawful activities, such as phone hacking.
The full extent of the payments due to Associated was not announced on Friday. If it cannot be agreed between the parties, Associated's costs will be assessed in separate proceedings.
JUDGMENT COMES AS HARRY IS SET TO MOVE BACK TO UK
The ruling comes days after the surprise news that Harry, who stepped down from official duties in 2020, will return with his wife Meghan and their two children to live in Britain from their current home in California.
Nicklin, explaining the decision on costs, was highly critical of the way the claimants' case had been put, including that serious allegations had rested on "speculative and inferential" foundations and had not been withdrawn when they were no longer being pursued.
"In my judgment, the cumulative effect of these matters takes the case well outside the norm. The conduct was unreasonable to a high degree," Nicklin said.
A spokesman for Associated Newspapers called the ruling "another overwhelming victory for the Mail and its journalism". There was no comment from Harry's spokesperson.
In July, Harry called the dismissal of the lawsuit "a complete and obvious whitewash".
The prince, 41, has long blamed the press for the 1997 Paris car crash that killed his mother, Princess Diana, and compared her treatment to that of his American wife Meghan. Holding back tears in the witness box in January, he said the Daily Mail had made Meghan's life "an absolute misery".
He had previously won against the publisher of the Daily Mirror tabloid and had settled a claim with Rupert Murdoch's British newspaper arm, but the latest ruling is a significant defeat in his battles with the media.
CLAIMANTS' INSURANCE POLICY FALLS SHORT OF ESTIMATED COSTS
The court was told at a hearing in July that Associated had incurred a legal bill of £34.5 million (US$45.8 million), while Harry and other claimants only had an insurance policy which covered £16 million.
Associated's lawyer Antony White argued the claimants had made wide-ranging and serious, "egregious" allegations without supporting evidence which had added to their costs.
He also said Harry's statement following the ruling was an abuse of his position and celebrity status.
Nicholas Bacon, the lawyer for the claimants, said in their submissions that Associated's £34.5 million legal bill was "eye-watering", far exceeding an agreed budget.
In his ruling rejecting Harry and the others' lawsuits following an 11-week trial, Nicklin said the claimants had needed to prove that information published about them had been obtained unlawfully. He said they had failed to do so and that suspicion alone was not enough.
No decision has yet been made on whether the claimants will appeal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Terengganu Perhilitan probes wild elephant sighting, residents advised to stay away
Article:
KUALA NERUS: The Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) is investigating a complaint about a wild elephant reportedly roaming in Kampung Pengkalan Gelugor, Jeram, here yesterday.
State Perhilitan director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said investigations found that the elephant had destroyed residents' crops, including banana and sugarcane plants, while roaming around the village and posing a safety risk to residents.
He advised members of the public not to enter the affected area or approach the elephant to prevent any untoward incidents.
"Residents must not follow the elephant's tracks, throw objects at it or take any action that could provoke it, and must give way if the animal crosses their path.
"Residents are also urged to give the department space to carry out control and translocation operations when conditions permit," he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, he said the nearest forest reserve to the location of the incident was the Belara Forest Reserve in Kuala Nerus, but there had been no previous records of elephant sightings in the area.
He added that police and other security agencies had been informed and were also assisting in controlling traffic and the movement of residents in the area.
"Perhilitan is also carrying out control and monitoring around the location of the complaint before translocation action is taken when conditions are suitable," he said.

Title: Police record Hadi's statement over his article, says aide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have recorded a statement from Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang over one of his articles, his aide said.
His political secretary, Mohd Syahir Sulaiman, told the New Straits Times that the Marang member of Parliament had his statement recorded in Kuala Lumpur last week.
Syahir, who is also Pas assistant secretary-general, said police launched an investigation into Hadi following reports lodged by DAP supporters.
"There were a few reports lodged by DAP supporters against one of Hadi's articles.
"He had his statement recorded in Kuala Lumpur last week. He also provided his full cooperation to assist in the police investigation.
"He is also ready to answer in court if there are grounds to charge him," Syahir said.
Syahir did not specify the article in question, but it is believed to be one of Hadi's columns published under his 'Minda Presiden Pas' column.
The NST has reached out to the police for comments,

Title: Comfort zone keeping Bumiputera firms off Bursa, says PNB chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A lack of strategic planning to scale Bumiputera companies remains the primary barrier preventing them from being listed on Bursa Malaysia, says the head of one of the country's largest fund management companies.
Permodalan Nasional Bhd president and group chief executive Datuk Rizal Rickman Ramli said many Bumiputera firms were reluctant to undertake bold transformation as they were comfortable operating as they were.
He said access to capital and loans in Malaysia was readily available, but many firms lacked the drive to advance to the next level.
"There are ample funding and loan opportunities in Malaysia. What is lacking is perhaps the vision and ambition to move towards a public listing, as well as partners who can assist through value-creation plans," he said in an interview.
Rizal said some entrepreneurs put growth aspirations on the back burner once their businesses performed well and reached a comfort zone.
However, he said scaling up required significant operational shifts, including institutionalising business processes and bringing in professional management.
He also cited succession planning as a major hurdle, with founders often wishing to pass businesses to family members who might not be interested in managing them.
This gap, Rizal said, created room for institutional investors to step in as advisers under the 10 Bumiputera Champions Programme, helping build stronger and more resilient corporate structures.
Partnering with major institutional investors also allowed entrepreneurs to receive guidance and discuss strategic growth decisions, he said.
"Entrepreneurs have PNB, the Employees Provident Fund and other government-linked investment companies to consult on expansion plans.
"Businessmen often have many ideas, but focusing on the right ones is key," he said.
PNB is among six government-linked investment companies participating in the Government-Linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme, which aims to drive strategic investments, nurture high-potential companies and broaden socio-economic impact across government-linked company networks.
Bumiputera empowerment remains a core priority under the initiative.
In 2025, GLICs invested RM1.3 billion directly into Bumiputera companies to support their expansion. GLCs and Petronas procured an annual average of about RM49 billion in goods and services from Bumiputera businesses between 2022 and 2025.

Title: Haze: 10 Sarawak areas record unhealthy API readings, Serian highest at 191
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ten areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 7.30am today, with Serian recording the highest reading at 191.
Based on the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas registering unhealthy API readings included Kuching (181), Samarahan (178), Sri Aman (174) and Sarikei (171).
The other areas were Sibu (160); Samalaju, Bintulu and Mukah (156); and Miri (151).
Bukit Rambai in Melaka was the only area outside Sarawak to record an unhealthy API reading, at 140.
Yesterday, 591 schools under 10 District Education Offices (PPDs) in Sarawak were ordered to close due to deteriorating air quality caused by transboundary haze.
The affected schools are under the Kuching, Padawan, Bau, Lundu, Samarahan, Simunjan, Serian, Sri Aman, Lubok Antu and Betong PPDs.
The Department of Environment (DOE) said the Regional Haze Map issued by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) showed continued dry weather conditions across most of the southern Asean region, except for rainfall over northeastern Borneo and northern Sumatra.
Hotspots were detected extensively in Kalimantan, while isolated hotspots were detected in other parts of the region. Moderate to dense transboundary smoke plumes were observed in West Kalimantan and moving northwards into western Sarawak.
The DOE said it had stepped up enforcement operations and daily patrols in areas at risk of open burning, while monitoring API readings.
The National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan have also been activated to coordinate government agencies' efforts to tackle open burning and respond to haze conditions nationwide.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.

Title: #NSTviral: Netizens urge DBKL action over stall blocking Sentul walkway
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Netizens have urged Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to take swift enforcement action against an unauthorised street stall in Kampung Batu, Sentul, after it obstructed a public five-foot walkway.
Threads user @bungaeomma posted photos highlighting the safety hazards and inconvenience caused to pedestrians by the stall.
In the viral post, the user questioned the trader's decision to operate in a manner that could compromise public safety and pedestrian access.
"Trade properly and legally without disturbing others," the user wrote.
"Not only do you block the entire road for pedestrians, but even the oil spill has made the road slippery and muddy. Moreover, the iron fences that were installed are being removed at will by the traders," the user said in another post.
Bungaeomma also said she had submitted a complaint to DBKL through ADU@KL.
"The new pedestrian path has just been upgraded by the government. The moss hasn't even had time to grow, but it's already filled with cooking oil. Sadly, public assets are treated like this. Who else will take care of Malaysia if not the Malaysian people themselves?" she wrote.
The post sparked concern online, with users condemning the operator for allegedly setting up the stall without authorisation and spilling grease onto the pedestrian walkway.
Netizens also called on DBKL's enforcement department to take action against the stall and issue compounds against unauthorised traders occupying public walkways.
Threads user @hazzbays97 said: "OK, I'm going to file a report. I can't stand seeing things like this. Malaysia will never progress as long as people think like this."
Another user, @hnissofiaa_iman, said: "Shouldn't be, foreigners or what? Better just pick up people like this."
User @ohmeelo said: "Sentul folk, please report this en masse to DBKL. Damage to public property will take time to repair and waste funds. Do not compromise on illegal hawkers, especially those operating on pedestrian walkways."

Title: Technology, construction to gain as expanded FBM KLCI cuts bank, utility weights [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The expansion of the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) is set to dilute the dominance of banking and utilities, with technology, construction and consumer sectors emerging as the key beneficiaries, analysts said.
The shift to 50 stocks should avoid an over concentration on the heavyweights in the bank, energy and telecommunication sectors, they added.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said technology is expected to be the biggest winner among the new sectors entering the FBM KLCI following its expansion from December 2026.
The sector is projected to account for 1.9 per cent of the index weighting in phase one and 3.4 per cent in phase two, from no representation currently.
"For existing sectors already present in the FBM KLCI, construction appears to be the largest gainer, with its weight increasing by 82 basis points (bp) to 151bp, based on our calculations.
"Conversely, our projections show that the most notable decline in weights will come from banking (338bp to 621bp) and utilities (140bp to 257bp).
"We estimate that the weights of sectors such as consumer, healthcare, oil and gas, plantation, property, and telco will remain relatively unchanged," it said in a note.
BANKING DILUTION
MBSB Research said financial services are expected to retain the largest weighting in the FBM KLCI, although their share will be reduced.
Based on its estimates, the sector's weighting is expected to decline by 5.85 percentage points, from 41.88 per cent currently to 36.03 per cent by the second tranche.
"The utilities sector is expected to decline by 2.60 percentage points from 16.83 per cent to 14.23 per cent by tranche two.
"Sectors that will now receive a fairer representation are technology, from 0 per cent to 3.21 per cent, and consumer products and services, rising from 4.44 per cent to 6.91 per cent," MBSB Research said.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd is positive on the expansion, expecting it to provide a more representative benchmark of the Malaysian equity market, reduce concentration in large-cap sectors and broaden industry representation.
Based on its simulation using share prices as at Aug 20, the firm said expanding the FBM KLCI to 50 constituents would lower the weighting of financial services to about 36.8 per cent from 42.8 per cent and utilities to 15.8 per cent from 18.8 per cent.
At the same time, the expansion would increase the representation and weighting of sectors including real estate, industrials, energy, consumer and technology, it said.
The FBM KLCI will be expanded from 30 to 50 constituents from December 2026.
At the same time, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Mid 70 Index will be reduced to 50 constituents and renamed the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Mid Cap Index.
The expansion will be carried out in two phases, starting on Dec 21 this year. In the first phase, 20 new stocks will be added to the FBM KLCI at half their final index weight.
In the second phase, the 20 new constituents will reach their full index weight, completing the transition to the expanded FBM KLCI on June 21 next year.
This will be the first major revamp of the FBM KLCI since July 2009, when the index was cut from 100 to 30 stocks.
HLIB acknowledged that the two-phase implementation would allow market participants to adjust gradually, but said it could also prolong the potential overhang on the existing 30 KLCI constituents.
"Investors may not be inclined to add positions to these stocks given the inevitable weight reduction over the two phases, a timeline that stretches until mid-2027.
"We estimate that the cumulative weighting of the KLCI's existing members would be diluted from 100 per cent currently to 91.3 per cent in phase one and 84 per cent in phase two," it added.
RHB Research said the existing 30 constituents account for about 84 per cent of the expanded 50-stock index, based on the proforma changes.
The biggest losers are the banking and energy sectors, with their weightings expected to fall by about five percentage points and 2.4 percentage points respectively, the firm noted.
Automotive, REITs, technology, gaming and transport will gain representation.
RHB Research said technology is expected to have the largest new weighting at about three per cent followed by transport at 1.6 per cent and gaming at 1.2 per cent.
The construction sector will also see its weighting increase by about one percentage point, following the inclusion of IJM Corp Bhd and Sunway Construction Bhd.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran threatens military response to US sanctions
Article:
DUBAI: Iran said on Friday that its response to any new US threats would be "devastating" after Washington pledged to impose the toughest financial penalties in history with the aim of toppling the Iranian leadership.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he would give details on Monday of the planned sanctions, after President Donald Trump warned of economic consequences against any country that provided "any type of lifeline to Iran".
The chief of staff of Iran's Armed Forces, Major General Ali Abdollahi, said the Islamic Republic's reaction would be broad and decisive.
"With preparedness across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace, Iran's armed forces will respond to the enemy's new threats with crushing, punishing and devastating responses," Abdollahi was quoted as saying by Iranian media.
Iranian leaders and Trump alike have issued triumphant and threatening statements even as each side has yet to prevail in the war that the US and Israel started nearly six months ago, killing thousands of people while drawing in other Gulf nations and pushing up global fuel prices.
US attacks have severely diminished Iran's economy and its conventional forces, but Teheran maintains enough missile and drone capability to impede oil tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and attack regional rivals.
AN UNPOPULAR WAR
Trump, meanwhile, has yet to achieve objectives he set at the start of the war, such as dismantling Iran's nuclear programme and creating conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers.
The war has driven up gas prices and weighed heavily on his popularity, which fell to the lowest point in his current term in a Reuters/Ipsos poll this week.
Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, the country's main negotiator in mediated talks with the US, said Washington appeared to have concluded it could not prevail in its direct military confrontation.
"We must make plans to deal with the unjust sanctions so that we can overcome them," he said in neighbouring Iraq.
But, speaking to Iranian and Iraqi businesspeople late on Thursday, Qalibaf acknowledged the strain on Iran's economy.
"No matter how much military power we have, we won't survive if people are hungry and we don't have financial turnover, economic growth and national production," Qalibaf said, according to official news agency IRNA.
[[nid:1516358]]
OIL UP ON SANCTIONS THREAT
International and US crude oil futures rose on Friday after the US threatened economic sanctions on Iran's trading partners, raising expectations of tighter supply in the coming weeks.
Bessent told CNBC he would provide details on the new sanctions at a press conference on Monday, adding, "We are going to collapse this regime."
Iran has weathered near-continuous economic sanctions for nearly 50 years, since the Islamic Revolution of 1979, but its people are suffering high inflation, a weakening currency and energy shortages along with damaged infrastructure.
Tighter sanctions could have wider international implications.
Bessent said China got half its energy from the Gulf, so it would make sense for them to "get with the programme".
China buys more than 80 per cent of Iran's shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler, but further US economic warfare with Beijing, which has eased earlier restrictions on exports of its vital rare-earth minerals, risks retaliation.
China's embassy in Washington said, "Sanctions and pressure do not help resolve the problem" and called for diplomacy.
There are other risks, especially to US allies in the Gulf, some of whose energy facilities and the desalination plants they depend on for drinking water have come under Iranian attack.
The US and Iran have twice announced ceasefire deals, in April and June, aiming to restore the free flow of ships through Hormuz, which before February carried about a fifth of all traded oil.
Iran and Oman, which lies just across the narrow strait, have been in separate talks with a stated purpose to resume navigation, but the US has opposed any deal that would impose a toll on ships.
Nato's top commander, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, convened a videoconference of allies at the chief of defence level on Wednesday to discuss ways to support freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, his spokesperson told Reuters on Friday.
The spokesperson said the effort was not a Nato mission but, given the alliance's capabilities, "it makes sense for Nato to facilitate in this way."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US Supreme Court allows White House ballroom construction for now
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US Supreme Court on Friday allowed construction of a massive White House ballroom to continue for now, giving President Donald Trump a temporary victory for one of his pet renovation projects.
Chief Justice John Roberts temporarily lifted a lower court ruling that had demanded a halt to construction of the controversial ballroom by midnight on Friday.
Roberts's one-sentence order means work on the ballroom, which has been challenged by historical preservation groups, may proceed while litigation plays out in the lower courts.
Trump, in a post on Truth Social, said he was "grateful" for the Supreme Court decision.
"The Military/Ballroom Complex being built on the hallowed grounds of the White House, which is so vital for National Security, will be the greatest of its kind!" he said. "Construction is under budget and ahead of schedule."
The Trump administration asked the conservative-dominated Supreme Court last week to allow it to finish building the ballroom and an underground bunker at the White House, saying the project was essential for national security.
Trump ordered the demolition of the entire historic East Wing of the White House last year – without input from Congress – to make way for his long-desired ballroom, but the project was quickly challenged in court.
A district court ordered a halt to work on the above-ground ballroom while allowing construction of the underground military bunker to proceed, but that order had been stayed while on appeal.
The appellate court recently upheld the lower court's order, agreeing that such a sweeping White House overhaul required the explicit consent of Congress, but gave the administration time to appeal to the Supreme Court.
Trump initially touted the construction of the ballroom as being necessary to host galas and state dinners, but has since repeatedly emphasised the addition of a sophisticated underground military bunker and other security features.
'NOT A TENANT'
Solicitor General John Sauer, in the appeal to the Supreme Court, also stressed the security aspects of the project and argued that the president has the authority to make changes to the White House.
"The President of the United States of America is not a tenant, but rather the sole, elected head of the Executive Branch, and Congress has authorised him to renovate, secure, and protect the White House and its grounds, as other Presidents have been allowed to do, without exception," Sauer said.
The project is already 65 per cent complete, he said, and halting it "will stall this vital construction, making this president – the subject of recurrent assassination attempts – much less safe, and risking future presidents' safety."
Work on the ballroom began last year with the sudden demolition of the East Wing, which used to house the offices of the First Lady.
Trump has insisted that the ballroom will be privately financed, but according to media reports, significant taxpayer funds are going to the project, which could cost as much as US$600 million.
The ballroom is just one of Trump's moves to leave his mark on Washington by the time his second term ends in January 2029. They include renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, a White House helipad, work on public parks and plans to construct a gigantic downtown arch.
Several of the projects have similarly faced legal challenges, but the ballroom project is the first to reach the Supreme Court.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang coastline needs early action as erosion risks grow
Article:
KUANTAN: Pahang's direct exposure to South China Sea makes its coastline increasingly vulnerable to stronger waves and extreme weather, highlighting the need for early action to tackle coastal erosion.
Universiti Malaysia Terengganu  Associate Professor  Dr Effi Helmy Ariffin said unlike parts of Terengganu where offshore islands provided some protection from the open sea, Pahang's coastline was more directly exposed to severe weather.
"There can be typhoons, cyclones and other  extreme weather events. The effects of coastal erosion are gradual but becoming increasingly visible, particularly along the southern part of Pahang.
"Pekan, including Nenasi and Rompin, are among the areas showing signs of coastal erosion."
The coastal erosion expert said early intervention was vital because timely action could prevent more serious and costly damage in the future.
He  proposed a hybrid approach combining breakwaters and artificial reefs.
He described it as the best way forward given the difficulty of predicting conditions in the South China Sea.
"The hybrid concept involves positioning the reefs between the breakwaters.
"For long-term planning, we need a more sustainable approach, while short-term measures can include armour rock or other forms of coastal protection."
Effi Helmy also highlighted the role of sediment movement in maintaining beaches, particularly when sand was removed from river estuaries for flood mitigation and navigation.
"Sand obtained through dredging could be considered for replenishing beaches affected by erosion, subject to proper   assessment of the sediment's suitability.
"Soft solutions such as beach nourishment can be adopted alongside other coastal protection measures."
Environmentalist Dr Muhamad Rusdi Ahmad Rusmili said studies of coastal and river-mouth hydrodynamics (the movement of water) were crucial to understanding and managing coastal erosion, as changes in water flow could affect sediment movement and accelerate shoreline loss.
The Malaysian Nature Society (MNS) Pahang branch chairman said seemingly minor factors could have significant consequences for coastal areas, making it important to examine water movement, river systems and the interaction between waves, sediment and the coastline.
He said Pahang's east coast was particularly vulnerable during the northeast monsoon, when strong winds and waves could transport sand offshore and intensify coastal erosion.
"Beserah is among the areas at risk of  coastal erosion.
"Concrete barriers and wave breakers could offer protection in certain circumstances, but such measures should  be implemented only after  studies are conducted to assess their potential effects on surrounding areas.
"Development is necessary, but it has to be done properly. We do not want a situation where protecting one area causes problems somewhere else."
Rusdi said environmental impact assessments and other technical studies should consider a broad range of factors before coastal development projects are allowed to proceed.
These should include hydrodynamics, sediment movement, river discharge, wave patterns and the potential impact of coastal structures on neighbouring stretches of coastline.
He said an  understanding of these factors would help ensure that efforts to protect vulnerable areas did not inadvertently worsen erosion elsewhere.
Rusdi said MNS carried out mangrove restoration and coastal tree-planting programmes where conditions were suitable, particularly where mangroves could help stabilise the shoreline and reduce erosion.
"Not every coastal area is suitable for mangrove planting, as the success of restoration depends on factors such as soil conditions, water movement and the characteristics of river mouths."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang seeks RM850m to tackle erosion along 61km coastline
Article:
KUANTAN: The Pahang government has implemented short- and long-term measures to address coastal erosion  along  61km of coastline in the Pekan, Rompin and Kuantan districts.
State Public Works, Transport and Health Committee chairman Datuk  Razali Kassim said the  Irrigation and Drainage Department  conducted studies and kept records to identify the   causes of coastal erosion and determine  appropriate measures.
He said coastal erosion was a year-round issue requiring continuous monitoring and action, particularly  where it could affect  homes, public infrastructure and access routes.
"Various engineering approaches are being considered, depending on the conditions
and characteristics of each location.
"Some problems can be resolved quickly, while major works will take longer.
"At some locations, temporary repairs and mitigation measures have  been carried out to prevent further damage while longer-term solutions are being  considered."
He said the Pahang Integrated Shoreline Management Plan, led by the Irrigation and Drainage Department and completed last year, identified several factors contributing to coastal erosion.
These included  development activities, sand mining, the natural loss of sandbars and mud,  mangrove loss and large waves coinciding with high tides.
Razali said some stretches of the coastal road between Pekan and Rompin, including Padang Api-Api in Nenasi, had been affected by erosion.
"Apart from short-term measures to address the worsening  erosion along the stretch, we are also considering  realigning the road as part of long-term infrastructure improvements."
He said the Pahang government, through the Irrigation and Drainage Department, had requested  RM850 million under the 13th Malaysia Plan for coastal erosion control, estuary conservation and related mitigation works.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Waves sweep away home, memories in Rompin village [WATCH]
Article:
ROMPIN:   The Malay proverb, "
kalau takut dilambung ombak, jangan berumah di tepi pantai
" (if you are afraid of being hit by waves, do not live by the beach), has taken on a painful meaning for Nur Zakiah Hamdan, whose family lost their home in Kampung Jawa here to coastal erosion last year.
The three-room house was sponsored by a financial institution for her family in 2009. They did not expect giant waves during the monsoon season on Jan 12 last year to bring down one of its walls, forcing them to leave the village.
The 30-year-old said the incident had a profound impact on her family, especially her father, Hamdan Mohid, 61, who would shed tears each time he visited the damaged house, now riddled with cracks and rusting window frames.
"Our home held so many memories. It had a verandah facing the sea where my whole family would spend our evenings watching the waves and enjoying the sea breeze... it was where my youngest brother was born, and where I lost my mother and a brother to illness.
"Everything was taken away in a single night, when the waves repeatedly crashed against the walls, sweeping away our furniture and electrical appliances.
"Just hours earlier, we were told to move to a nearby relief centre with several neighbours," she said when met recently.
The housewife said the house might have been spared if preventive measures had been taken earlier to slow the erosion.
"When I moved here, the shoreline was about 500m from my house. During the incident last year, the sea was barely 20m away. The huge casuarina trees and the tarred road in front of my house have disappeared.
"Over the years, the  trees collapsed one after another due to the powerful waves before the road was eventually swept away.
"Sadly, no erosion barrier was built until last year, when geotubes were placed along the coastline... it was already too late," she said.
Nur Zakiah, who now lives in a rented house in the nearby Kampung Janglau, said she still vividly remembered the night her family's home was damaged.
She was at the relief centre  on the night of Jan 12 last year when her husband told her  the walls of their house had collapsed.
"I went back to inspect the house. The electricity had been shut off and most of our belongings had been washed away by the strong waves. Luckily, we managed to rescue some documents before moving to the relief centre," she said, adding that losses were estimated at more than RM20,000.
Azman Jumahir, who lives in the same village, said villagers used to be wary of huge waves only during the monsoon season, but now they had to be on alert  throughout the year, especially during high tide.
The 30-year-old, who grew up in the village, said such incidents had become more frequent over the past few years, with huge waves sweeping debris and plastic bottles into the settlement.
"During high tide, the waves enter my house, which is about 100m from the shoreline. Since 2023, we have been told to evacuate during the monsoon season... not because of floods, but because of huge waves," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM700,000 seaside dream swept away by coastal erosion [WATCH]
Article:
PEKAN:    A businessman's dream of turning a stretch of the coast in Tanjung Batu here into a unique seaside retreat was all but swept away by the relentless advance of the sea.
Tourism entrepreneur Edde Firdaus Abdul Aziz had invested some RM700,000 to acquire 1ha of coastal land, transforming it into Kekunang Tering Chalet, a nature getaway featuring seven chalets, including a tree house and tube cabins fashioned from concrete culverts.
But the dream lasted only about six years before relentless coastal erosion claimed the structures one by one.
The chalet units were swept into the sea in late 2022.
Edde Firdaus, 46, said the sea had since devoured much of the land, leaving just 0.4ha, with the remaining ground continuing to disappear.
"It's heartbreaking to see the chalet units disappear one by one. I only managed to operate the business for about six years before it was all swept away.
"Now, only the concrete culverts remain visible, partially buried in sand. The four concrete rooms were built furthest from the shoreline, so you can imagine the extent of the destruction," he said.
Edde Firdaus said after securing the land, he spent close to half a million ringgit on premium construction materials, including high-quality glass and furniture.
"I managed to salvage some furniture, electrical appliances and mattresses, but the structures were washed away. I never imagined that the land could disappear like this.
"When I bought the land, the ground was covered in grass, acacia trees and mangroves, while the shoreline was quite a distance away.
"Even when erosion began, I tried various methods, including placing giant sandbags to hold back the sea, but when the tree house collapsed, I knew trouble was closing in," he said.
Edde Firdaus claimed the beach erosion-control project in nearby Kampung Tanjung Batu, completed in March, appeared to have accelerated erosion along his property.
"Perhaps changes in the wave pattern and water flow contributed to the severe erosion. In the past, coastal erosion usually happened during the monsoon season, but now it happens throughout the year.
"I am just  waiting for the monsoon season this year. The extreme weather could wipe out what remains of my land," he said.
Former staff member Abdul Manan Md Amin, 61, who accompanied the
New Straits Times
to the site, said the chalets were unoccupied when they were washed away.
"It had been forecast that there would be high tide that night, so I was monitoring the site. The waves kept pounding the chalets and, the following morning, we saw that most of the structures had been washed away," he said.

Title: Trump announces temporary tariff relief on ground beef imports
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump announced on Friday that the United States would temporarily allow a greater volume of foreign beef imports, in his latest bid to lower costs for American consumers as midterm elections approach.
The US cattle herd has shrunk to its lowest level since the 1950s – in part due to drought and international competition – with the diminishing numbers pushing beef product prices higher.
"As we work to rebuild this herd and help our ranchers, for the next 90 days, the United States will allow up to 300,000 metric tons of product for ground beef to be imported with no out-of-quota tariff," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
The US president did not say which countries would be exporting the beef, but added there was a commitment to sell it at 25 per cent below market prices.
Steeper beef prices have become a symbol of high living costs in the world's biggest economy, pressing the Trump administration to take steps to bring costs down.
Affordability will be a key issue in November's midterm elections, where Democrats are seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Trump's Republicans.
'DISAPPOINTED'
US cattle and rancher groups have been resistant to importing more beef. Responding to the move, Senator Deb Fischer of Nebraska, a major beef-producing state, said she was "extremely disappointed".
"We all want lower grocery prices, but as I've said for months, we cannot do it at the expense of American producers. Flooding the market with foreign beef hurts our livestock industry," said Fischer, a Republican.
[[nid:1516327]]
Responding to the criticism later in the day, Trump offered no details on how the plan would work but insisted that he would get beef prices down because "that's what the voters want, and that's what I want".
Last fall, Trump demanded that ranchers slash their prices, and he later moved to expand imports of beef trimmings from Argentina to cool ground beef prices.
He has also launched an investigation into the meatpacking industry over the high prices of red meat.
His latest effort comes as American households struggle with stubborn inflation, fuelled by an energy crisis linked to the war on Iran.
Trump launched the war alongside ally Israel in late February, with Teheran's retaliatory action virtually blocking the Strait of Hormuz, a vital energy and fertiliser supply route.
This has pushed up fuel, transport and food costs, squeezing consumers.
Despite higher beef prices, US consumer demand for meat remains robust.
The US Department of Agriculture estimates that total beef consumption this year will hit 29.4 billion pounds, an uptick from 2025.
The American Farm Bureau Federation warned in May, however, that Americans are consuming more beef than US farmers and ranchers can supply.
It added that ranchers need to rebuild the US cattle herd – or demand would have to cool – in order for beef prices to fall.
Yet "cattle producers still face substantial uncertainty that clouds herd rebuilding decisions," Bernt Nelson, an economist at the federation, wrote.
These include threats to animal health, including the New World screwworm, a flesh-eating parasite.
